verdict.rationale: Kong AI Gateway documents inbound authentication through AI Auth Strategies attached to AI Models or Agents, an AI Rate Limiting Advanced plugin, and per-request cost calculation that it says underpins "budget enforcement, per-consumer spend limits". Together these approximate a credential with rate and spend guardrails, but the evidence never shows the end-to-end flow of issuing an agent its own key with a hard spend cap. missing for 10: explicit per-agent API key issuance, documented configuration of a hard budget or spend cap that blocks requests, details on token- or cost-based rate limit enforcement per consumer, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an autonomous agent its own key with budget and rate guardrails so it cannot run away on spend

citations.quote: Cost is one of the primary signals AI governance acts on: budget enforcement, per-consumer spend limits, and chargeback all depend on an accurate cost figure for each request.
An AI Auth Strategy lets you declare an inbound authentication mechanism at the gateway level and attach it to specific AI Models, AI Agents, or AI MCP Servers.
